topic: Certified mixed-variable neural-SCM identified-set inference via a response-function outer sieve: for a known acyclic ADMG and compact class with finite district response labels, bounded-density continuous district noise, Lipschitz continuous mechanisms, and inverse-CDF categorical mechanisms, construct an exact-multinomial finite-sample outer interval and neural feasible inner interval; prove uniform coverage of the entire restricted identified set, an excess-width decomposition into the graph-query endpoint modulus evaluated at sampling radius plus explicit O(h) sieve error and a rationally verified epsilon global-optimization gap, and finite-h termination of spatial branch-and-bound with independently checkable certificates; include the uniform binary bow witness and the UA-DCM Parents' Labor Supply and Autobounds consumers

open_problems.open_problem: Can exact multinomial inversion give finite-sample uniform coverage of the entire restricted identified set of a latent-confounded mixed-variable neural SCM after explicit sieve and optimization enlargement?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves asymptotic consistency for mixed continuous-categorical NCM bounds and leaves finite-sample guarantees under unobserved confounding as future work.
source_refs.author: Jiyuan Tan, Jose Blanchet, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs nonasymptotic multinomial confidence regions with controlled coverage for arbitrary finite dimension.
source_refs.author: Djalil Chafaï, Didier Concordet
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper gives uniformly asymptotically valid confidence regions for identified sets rather than exact finite-sample coverage.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano, Azeem M. Shaikh

source_refs.excerpt: The multinomial-proportion Gaussian limit has mean p and covariance diag(p)-pp^T.
The core does not assert a singular-covariance version.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis identify finite-sample guarantees as a missing step and attribute the difficulty to the geometry of the bound-defining optimization program; their finite-sample result excludes unobserved confounding. The prior CausalSmith review validates multinomial CLT and directional-delta ingredients but explicitly withholds the singular-covariance extension. Neither those asymptotic tools nor existing exact multinomial regions have been propagated through the nonsmooth latent-SCM compatibility map to cover every value in the restricted identified set. The proof must begin with exact observable-law coverage and deterministic set inclusion, rather than endpoint differentiation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact multinomial region C_n and optimized interval I_n satisfying inf_M Pr_M{Theta(P_M) is a subset of I_n} >= 1-alpha for every n, together with an excess-width bound omega_Q(r_n)+C_sieve h+2 epsilon_opt.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction moves cleanly from neural partial-identification practice to the missing finite-sample guarantee and separates representation, sampling, and optimization errors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Neural SCMs automate mixed-variable causal bounds -> current theory establishes representation and asymptotic consistency -> latent-confounded finite-sample whole-set coverage remains unresolved

method_exemplars.technique: Encode SCM compatibility and the causal query as a constrained endpoint-optimization problem over response-function distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired interval is the image of an exact uncertainty set for the observable law under the same causal endpoint optimization.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert likelihood-level covering collections to obtain a finite-sample multinomial confidence region with controlled coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite observable response categories make the statistical input multinomial, allowing exact coverage to be inherited through deterministic causal optimization.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct random regions covering the full identified set and prove uniform validity over a class of data-generating processes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the correct whole-set inferential target, while the proposed resolution replaces its asymptotic calibration with exact multinomial coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Does finite response-label discretization of bounded-density district noise produce an outer sieve for Lipschitz mixed-variable ADMG SCMs whose causal-query endpoint error is uniformly O(h), apart from the endpoint modulus of the induced observable-law perturbation?

source_refs.claim: Finite canonical response domains yield sharp polynomial-program bounds for discrete observed SCMs, but the construction assumes finite observed domains.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper states that canonical response partitioning does not extend practically to continuous settings because complexity grows with observed cardinality.
source_refs.author: Valentyn Melnychuk, Dennis Frauen, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: The paper proves mixed-variable NCM approximation in Wasserstein distance, including categorical mechanisms, but not a certifiable response-function outer sieve.
source_refs.author: Jiyuan Tan, Jose Blanchet, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.excerpt: Sufficiently large finite disturbance cardinalities preserve the canonical-DAG full-data-law model.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Canonical response-function enumeration is exact for finite observed domains, whereas continuous-outcome work identifies a cardinality barrier. Neural approximation handles mixed variables but does not outer-approximate every admissible SCM. The prior finite-disturbance reduction likewise supplies no quantitative discretization for continuous district noise or shared latent response labels. The first proof step that changes is canonical-partition equivalence: cellwise coupling must preserve district dependence, while bounded-density arguments control the boundary layers created by inverse-CDF categorical thresholds and graphwise Lipschitz propagation controls query error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every mesh h, a theorem constructing a finite response-label feasible set containing every admissible mixed SCM image and proving max{|q_h^+-q^+|,|q_h^--q^-|} <= omega_Q(delta_h)+C h with explicit graph-, density-, and Lipschitz-dependent constants.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing explains how canonical SCMs convert counterfactual bounding into finite optimization and naturally exposes the continuous-variable boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Counterfactual queries are often nonidentified -> finite canonical SCMs reduce discrete sharp bounds to polynomial programs -> mixed continuous districts require a quantitatively controlled outer canonicalization

method_exemplars.technique: Partition exogenous domains by finite response signatures and optimize the query polynomial over the resulting response-type masses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed sieve is a quantitative mixed-variable relaxation of this exact finite response-signature construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate local mechanism approximation through an acyclic SCM in topological order and translate distributional error into causal-query error under Lipschitz control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The O(h) result needs the same graphwise error propagation, with cell quantization replacing neural approximation and threshold-boundary mass treated separately.

method_exemplars.technique: Extremize a target over relaxed empirical constraints and calibrate the relaxation for uniform endpoint coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once finite, the sieve endpoints are projections of a constrained set, matching the calibrated-projection structure.

open_problems.open_problem: Can spatial branch-and-bound for mixed-variable neural response-sieve causal bounds be made finitely epsilon-terminating while emitting independently checkable rational certificates for every global endpoint gap?

source_refs.claim: Autobounds uses dual relaxations and spatial branch-and-bound to return guaranteed outer ranges and epsilon-sharpness for discrete causal polynomial programs.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper develops an exact-rational branch-and-bound solver with numerically safe dual bounds for mixed-integer linear programs.
source_refs.author: William Cook, Thorsten Koch, Daniel E. Steffy, Kati Wolter

source_refs.claim: The paper specifies sequentially checkable certificates for integer-programming results and an independent verifier.
source_refs.author: Kevin K. H. Cheung, Ambros Gleixner, Daniel E. Steffy

source_refs.excerpt: The construction supplies positive finite same-P(V) separating SCMs.
Sufficiently large finite disturbance cardinalities preserve the canonical-DAG full-data-law model.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Autobounds establishes anytime outer bounds and epsilon-sharpness but relies on numerical nonlinear optimization rather than a compact rational proof object independently checked from first principles. Exact-rational branch-and-bound certificates exist for MILP, while the reviewed SCM constructions produce existential finite models rather than rational nonlinear certificates. The missing step is a certificate calculus for nonlinear envelope bounds on each spatial box, including inverse-CDF thresholds and neural mechanisms, whose relaxation gap provably vanishes under subdivision of a compact parameter domain.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A soundness-and-termination theorem defining a rational certificate with the branch partition, feasible incumbents, and exact relaxation witnesses, proving that a standalone checker validates epsilon-tight lower and upper endpoint bounds after finitely many subdivisions.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames automated causal bounding around anytime validity and epsilon-sharpness, providing the natural narrative to strengthen from solver-reported to independently verified guarantees.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Applied causal assumptions create bespoke partial-ID programs -> spatial branch-and-bound supplies anytime outer bounds -> high-stakes use requires portable proof certificates rather than trust in one numerical run

method_exemplars.technique: Record branch-and-bound deductions as exact rational inference steps and validate them with a solver-independent checker.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal certificate has the same trust boundary but must add proof rules for nonlinear spatial relaxations.

method_exemplars.technique: Repair approximate dual LP solutions by projection and shifting to obtain exactly feasible rational dual bounds throughout a branch-and-bound tree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every spatial node needs a rigorous relaxation bound, and dual repair can convert fast floating-point relaxations into exact node certificates.

method_exemplars.technique: Build an exact finite-sample multinomial confidence region before optimizing a downstream target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Combining exact input coverage with rational global-optimality certificates produces a fully checkable causal confidence endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: Can neural causal partial identification yield a certified feasible inner interval for the mixed-variable restricted ADMG-SCM class while preserving district sharing, observational compatibility, Lipschitz restrictions, and inverse-CDF categorical semantics?

source_refs.claim: Implicit generative models handle continuous and discrete variables, but tight-bound convergence is proved only for linear SCMs and nonlinear results are empirical.
source_refs.author: Vahid Balazadeh Meresht, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Rahul G. Krishnan

source_refs.claim: Lipschitz-regularized NCM extrema are asymptotically consistent, but finite-sample optimization geometry remains unresolved.
source_refs.author: Jiyuan Tan, Jose Blanchet, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: NCMs encode graph-induced structural constraints and are expressive for causal identification, but expressivity alone does not certify feasibility or global optimization.
source_refs.author: Kevin Xia, Kai-Zhan Lee, Yoshua Bengio, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: Finite disturbance cardinalities preserve the canonical-DAG full-data-law model.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing neural methods obtain candidate extrema through nonconvex training. Their representation and asymptotic results do not make a trained model an independently validated witness satisfying every observational and structural constraint, while finite response-law representability does not imply density of a bounded neural class subject to exact district coupling. Inverse-CDF categorical thresholds are discontinuous, and independently approximating node mechanisms can destroy shared-latent semantics or compatibility. The missing first step is a constructive district-coupled approximation and feasibility checker controlling observational and query errors jointly.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive theorem producing endpoint witnesses M_- and M_+ with independently checked membership in the restricted confidence-feasible SCM class, proving [Q(M_-),Q(M_+)] lies inside the outer interval, and bounding its Hausdorff gap by sampling, sieve, neural-approximation, and optimization terms.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the closest mixed-variable theory and separates neural representability from learnability and optimization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Neural SCMs offer scalable mixed-variable causal bounds -> Lipschitz control yields asymptotic consistency -> practical endpoints still lack finite witnessed feasibility and certified distance to the sharp set

method_exemplars.technique: Construct NCMs with graph-compatible shared exogenous inputs so neural mechanisms preserve the SCM restrictions relevant to causal queries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A valid inner witness must first inhabit the correct district-coupled graph-constrained SCM class.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit piecewise-linear neural structure in a complete branch-and-bound verification procedure with explicit lower and upper output bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The witness checker must certify network outputs and constraint ranges rather than trust gradient-based training.

method_exemplars.technique: Fit an implicit generative SCM to observed data while optimizing causal-query extrema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest estimator construction for neural inner endpoints in mixed continuous-discrete causal graphs.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the UA-DCM sampling-versus-nonidentification decomposition be converted into an exact finite-sample, solver-certified decision rule for the Parents' Labor Supply IV design, including certification that additional observational sampling cannot reverse the selected action?

source_refs.claim: UA-DCM defines the decomposition through min-max and max-min neural optimization and applies it to Parents' Labor Supply, but describes recovery as approximate.
source_refs.author: Md Musfiqur Rahman, Ziwei Jiang, Hilaf Hasson, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: The application uses sibling-sex composition as an instrument for the effect of an additional child on parents' labor supply.
source_refs.author: Joshua D. Angrist, William N. Evans

source_refs.claim: The paper derives sharp population bounds for binary imperfect-compliance IV models but not the proposed exact finite-sample uncertainty decomposition.
source_refs.author: Alexander Balke, Judea Pearl
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: UA-DCM introduces the relevant nested max-min and min-max objects and reports a labor-supply analysis, but its decomposition is recovered approximately with neural models. Balke-Pearl sharpness addresses the population binary-IV model, and exact multinomial methods address observed cell probabilities, but the scan found no theorem coupling those pieces to certify both UA-DCM uncertainty components or the stronger decision statement that collecting unlimited additional data from the same observational design cannot alter the action ranking.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Exact finite-n outer and persistent-nonidentification intervals for the labor-supply IV multinomial table, simultaneous 1-alpha coverage of both nested targets, and a rationally verified sign-separation condition proving that further observational sampling alone cannot reverse the preferred action.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames the practical choice between collecting more observations and changing the study design and culminates in the Parents' Labor Supply application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite observational data mix sampling and structural uncertainty -> only sampling uncertainty shrinks with more of the same data -> a certified decomposition is needed to decide whether to sample more or redesign

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate binary response types and solve the induced linear programs to obtain sharp IV treatment-effect endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Parents' Labor Supply consumer has a binary instrument-treatment-outcome table whose persistent uncertainty is structurally analogous to imperfect compliance.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact multinomial tests to obtain a controlled-coverage region for the full observed probability vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sampling-uncertainty layer can be formed by optimizing UA-DCM's nested causal targets over this exact region.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate projection inference for extrema under estimated constraints with uniform asymptotic validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its target-calibrated endpoint logic is the nearest inferential analogue to UA-DCM's nested extrema.

literature_map:
Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2405.15673) prove mixed continuous-categorical NCM approximation and asymptotic partial-ID consistency, explicitly leaving finite-sample guarantees under confounding open.
Xia, Lee, Bengio, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2107.00793) establish NCM expressiveness and graph-compatible causal inference while separating expressivity from learnability.
Xia, Pan, and Bareinboim (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.00035) give sound-and-complete neural procedures for counterfactual identification, but not certified partial-ID endpoints.
Balazadeh, Syrgkanis, and Krishnan (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2210.08139) optimize partial-ID bounds with mixed-variable implicit generators; tight convergence is proved for linear SCMs and nonlinear evidence is empirical.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022, arXiv:2110.05690) show exact finite canonical response domains and polynomial sharp-bound programs for discrete observed SCMs.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (JASA 2024, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2023.2216909) provide Autobounds, anytime outer bounds, and epsilon-sharpness for discrete causal polynomial programs.
Melnychuk, Frauen, and Feuerriegel (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.01424) identify the cardinality barrier to canonical response-function methods for continuous outcomes and introduce a curvature sensitivity model.
Balke and Pearl (JASA 1997, DOI 10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074) provide foundational sharp response-type bounds for binary imperfect compliance.
Chafaï and Concordet (JASA 2009, arXiv:0805.1971) give controlled-coverage small-sample confidence regions for a multinomial probability vector.
Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (ISIT 2021, DOI 10.1109/ISIT45174.2021.9517964) characterize minimum-average-volume multinomial confidence sets, but not nonlinear causal identified-set images.
Romano and Shaikh (Econometrica 2010, DOI 10.3982/ECTA6706) establish uniform asymptotic confidence regions for identified sets; Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (Econometrica 2019, arXiv:1601.00934) calibrate projected endpoint inference.
Cook, Koch, Steffy, and Wolter (Mathematical Programming Computation 2013, DOI 10.1007/s12532-013-0055-6) and Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (IPCO 2017, arXiv:1611.08832) show exact-rational branch-and-bound and independently checkable MILP certificates.
Bunel et al. (JMLR 2020, arXiv:1909.06588) provide complete branch-and-bound verification for piecewise-linear neural networks, while Kaltofen et al. (JSC 2012, DOI 10.1016/j.jsc.2011.08.002) provide exact rational SOS identities for polynomial nonnegativity.
Rahman, Jiang, Hasson, and Kocaoglu (2026, arXiv:2601.22736) introduce UA-DCM's min-max/max-min uncertainty decomposition and the Parents' Labor Supply consumer, but recover the decomposition approximately with NCMs.
